QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_30

question.text: The standard SROI ratio is computed as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Social Return on Investment (SROI) is a monetisation-based evaluation method that expresses social, environmental and economic outcomes in monetary terms and then compares them to the cost of the intervention. The standard SROI ratio is Net Impact Value divided by Investment, where Net Impact Value is the gross monetised outcome adjusted for deadweight (what would have happened anyway), attribution (credit to other actors), drop-off (fade of outcomes over time) and displacement (outcomes produced at another group's expense). A ratio of at least 1:1 indicates that the intervention generated as much or more social value than the cost invested. The Trap: Gross outcome divided by number of beneficiaries (option B) is an average outcome per beneficiary, not a return ratio. Investment divided by Net Impact Value (option C) inverts the SROI formula. Total expenditure divided by total CSR pool (option D) is a CSR budgeting/compliance ratio and has nothing to do with social return. Note: The cited workbook pages (151, 158, 161 of the Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook) refer to monetisation / SROI as an approach and state that monetary reports should disclose calculations, estimates, assumptions, and an audit trail, but they do not, in the pages checked, write out the formula SROI = Net Impact Value / Investment or list the four named deductions used in the explanation. The framing above reflects general SROI methodology as adopted in the social-impact / monetisation literature.
